80875.subject: 📉 Hot CPI crashes crypto
80875.body:
———————————————————————————

## Top Stories

**BTC** $80,822 (-3.3%) | **ETH** $2,359 (-5.9%) | **SOL** $102 (-5.0%)

* Bitcoin falls [below $81K](https://www.chooserich.live/story/bitcoin-falls-long-liquidations-uxufhb7) as US September CPI rises [3.7%](https://x.com/TreeNewsFeed/status/2110347404268728440) year over year, above the 3.6% estimate

* S&P 500 falls [1.22%](https://x.com/BullTheoryio/status/2110424813676482652) to 7,710.43, its biggest drop in over two months — US stocks shed [$660B](https://x.com/BullTheoryio/status/2110389555706962038)

* Spot bitcoin ETFs see [$261.5M](https://www.chooserich.live/story/bitcoin-ether-etfs-outflows-aa3eicx) in net outflows

* White House says US is exploring ways to [accumulate more Bitcoin](https://www.chooserich.live/story/white-house-accumulate-bitcoin-da9ha2d)

* Polygon Labs completes Coinme buyout, gaining payments coverage in [48 US states](https://www.chooserich.live/story/polygon-labs-acquires-coinme-hzzpyh6)

* Strive raises [$500M](https://www.chooserich.live/story/strive-stock-offering-buy-bitcoin-bsdkauq) via new SATS preferred shares to buy more bitcoin

* Fed funds futures put [66% odds](https://x.com/bespokeinvest/status/2110439064373535129) on no rate hike at the October 28 FOMC

* BlackRock posts Q3 revenue of [$7.75B](https://x.com/wallstengine/status/2110309824000852266) and $205B in net inflows, beating estimates

* Anthropic tells investors it turned profitable in Q3 with revenue near [$17B](https://www.chooserich.live/story/anthropic-reports-profitability-revenue-ipo-si3vu82)

* Strive buys [$235M](https://www.chooserich.live/story/strive-buys-bitcoin-pexi6e2) worth of BTC

* Apple hits [$5T](https://x.com/barronsonline/status/2110476593810272559) market cap even as the rest of the tech trade falters

* TSMC posts record profit for a [sixth straight quarter](https://www.chooserich.live/story/tsmc-record-profit-ai-demand-7as9t4t) on AI demand

* Brooklyn DA and FBI shut down [241 crypto fraud sites](https://www.chooserich.live/story/fbi-brooklyn-da-crypto-scam-websites-2i9b77c) tied to Eastern Europe

* Reports claim Richard Heart was [arrested in Turkey](https://www.chooserich.live/story/richard-heart-arrested-turkey-86ae5ze)

Hey, it's Adrian! Inflation came in hot on Wednesday. US consumer prices rose 3.7% over the year in September, above the 3.6% economists expected, and core inflation rose 0.3% in a single month against 0.2% expected. Gasoline alone was up 9.1% in a month and did more than half of the work. Filling up the car has rarely been this expensive for a crypto portfolio. Bitcoin dropped from about $83.5k before the release to $80.4k and trades at $81.2k as I write this. That’s right inside the support zone between $80k and $81.5k, which has held on every daily close since September 21. Luckily under the surface the picture is better than the price. Demand from spot and futures buyers grew by about 69k BTC over 30 days, and the largest holders are adding. And this besides ETF selling for about $859 million since October 7, which enhanced the dip and has to be absorbed. In the Pulse I look at which crypto businesses still earned money through the downturn. Most lost around two thirds of their revenue. A few earned more. And in the Alpha section I explain why I bought the dip in Pons, what I make of Lighter’s challenge to Hyperliquid, and why Pearl stays on my watchlist for now. Let’s get into the broader picture and how to set up for the coming week: ️ ⚡ On today's Episode: 📈 Macro Update – September CPI came in at 3.7% against 3.6% expected, core rose 0.3% for the month. Bitcoin fell to $80.4k, right into its support at $80k–$81.5k, while ETFs pulled about $859 million since October 7. 🔊 Crypto Pulse – Across 227 protocols the median lost about 62% of its revenue in the downturn. Gold and stablecoin issuers, trading cards, RWAs and prediction markets earned more, and derivatives venues earn the most on crash days. 🐂 Alpha Insights – I bought the Pons dip at 2.15x sales against 4.45x for Pump on FDV. Lighter earns under 7% of Hyperliquid’s fees on 30% of its volume, with an unlock coming in December, and Pearl stays on my watchlist. The current state of the market. Start with inflation, because that’s what moved everything this week. September’s consumer price index came in at 3.7% year over year, up from 3.4% in August and above the 3.6% forecast. Core inflation, which leaves out food and energy, rose 0.3% for the month and 2.6% over the year, both a notch above expectations. Energy drove most of it. 80868.subject: DIFC Courts Bring Instant Verification to Court Orders on Avalanche
80868.body:
View this post on the web at https://www.team1.blog/p/difc-courts-bring-instant-verification

The Dubai International Financial Centre (DIFC) Courts have begun issuing court orders and hearing records with credentials on the Avalanche C-Chain. Designed and built by Deca4 Advisory, the system allows recipients to verify a document’s origin and check whether it has been altered. Verification takes seconds and is available to anyone who receives a document, anywhere in the world.
The system is particularly relevant for cross-border commercial disputes. Parties can choose DIFC Courts to resolve disputes through a clause in their contract, even if neither party has a connection to the UAE. When court documents are presented to banks, companies or authorities in other jurisdictions, recipients need to establish their authenticity.
Want to keep up with the latest in the Avalanche ecosystem? Subscribe to the Team1 blog and get our updates in your inbox weekly.
How it Works
The system uses a cryptographic hash, a digital fingerprint generated from a file’s contents. The process has two main steps:
Issuance: When the Courts issue a document through their existing digital infrastructure, its cryptographic hash is linked to a unique NFT-based credential recorded on the Avalanche C-Chain.
Verification: The recipient checks the file against the onchain credential. If a single character in the document has changed, the hash changes, and the verification fails.
The document itself remains offchain. No document content or confidential case information is recorded on Avalanche. The credential is strictly non-transferable, carries no monetary value, and cannot be traded.
What does Blockchain Add?
In general, a public blockchain can provide a record that recipients can check without relying solely on records held within the issuing organisation’s own systems. Information recorded on a blockchain is also designed to be difficult to alter retrospectively.
The system works with the Courts’ existing digital document infrastructure. Recipients can check a document against its blockchain credential without needing access to the Courts’ internal systems.
Digital signatures can also help verify a document’s origin and detect changes. Blockchain-based credentials are therefore one approach among several, rather than the only way to establish document authenticity.
A successful check confirms that the file matches the credential issued for it. It does not establish that the document’s contents are true or, by itself, confirm whether a court order remains legally in force.
Broader UAE Alignment
The deployment aligns with the objectives of the Dubai Digital Strategy and Dubai Economic Agenda D33. It also sits within a wider adoption of Avalanche technology across UAE public infrastructure. Separately, the Telecommunications and Digital Government Regulatory Authority (TDRA) is working with Deca4 Advisory and Ava Labs to bring Avalanche infrastructure into the UA
